posts.title: The New Economy of Attention
posts.excerpt: Why attention — not money — is the scarcest resource.
posts.content:
Every product competes for the same thing: a few seconds of a reader's time.

Attention is the new currency

Brands that earn attention earn loyalty. Brands that interrupt it churn it away.

The long game

The companies that win are the ones that respect the reader's time enough to be worth reading.

posts.title: Designing for Calm
posts.content:
The best interfaces feel calm. They are quiet, predictable and honest.

Less chrome, more content

Every decorative element is a small tax on the reader. Remove it where it does not earn its place.

Honest states

Loading, empty and error states should be designed, not defaulted. They are where the user notices whether the product respects them.

posts.title: The Rise of Slow Media
posts.excerpt: In an age of infinite scroll, depth is a feature.
posts.content:
The feed rewards novelty. Slow media rewards depth.

Why slow wins

Depth is harder to copy. A two-thousand-word essay cannot be replaced by a thread.

The promise of the magazine

The magazine format is not a throwback — it is a deliberate bet on the reader's time being well spent.
